text:
priya: heads-up — we got a support ticket where the sample app crashed on a 500 and logged "Internal server error" with no actionable type. customer couldn't decide whether to retry or surface to users. :confused:

sam_w: ugh. this is a classic DX trap. right now python SDK returns a generic ApiError with .status_code, but no typed subclass. makes handling awkward.

miguel: TS SDK is slightly better — we return an `error.code` string (e.g. `RATE_LIMIT`, `AUTH_INVALID`) but people still parse strings. parity is a mess across SDKs.

emily: can we standardize on typed exceptions + structured fields? proposal: map HTTP -> typed exc, include `retriable: bool`, `retry_after: int|null`, and original `request_id`. example: ```py
class AuthError(ApiError): pass
class RateLimitError(ApiError): retry_after: Optional[int]
class ServerError(ApiError): retriable = True
```

priya: +1. also need clear message text for onboarding — avoid vague "internal server error". include short human message and machine fields for programmatic logic.

miguel: compatibility concern: TS consumers use `.code` switch statements. we'd need a migration plan: emit both `error.code` and typed class for a transition window.

sam_w: agree. for retries, we should codify which errors are auto-retriable by default in SDKs (e.g., 502/503/504 with exponential backoff), and expose policy override. also need consistent auth errors: 401 -> AuthError (non-retriable), 403 -> PermissionError (non-retriable), 429 -> RateLimitError (retriable with `retry_after`).

emily: small sample mapping we can put in the spec: ```
HTTP 401 -> AuthError (retriable=false)
HTTP 403 -> PermissionError (retriable=false)
HTTP 408/429 -> RateLimitError (retriable=true, retry_after from header)
HTTP 500-599 -> ServerError (retriable=true for 502/503/504 else maybe false)
```

priya: also add an opt-in strict mode in SDK that raises on ambiguous 5xx instead of swallowing, to make onboarding easier for apps that want fail-fast.

miguel: tests: need cross-sdk test vectors (status, headers, body) and sample app that demonstrates recommended handling patterns. I can add a small harness in the samples repo.

sam_w: prioritization: low-latency fix = better messages in API (improve body to include `error.code`, `error.type`, `retriable`, `retry_after`, `request_id`). SDK work is medium priority (typed exceptions + default retry policies). docs + sample app = quick win.

emily: can we add a tiny snippet for consumers showing best practice? e.g., ```py
try:
    client.generate(...)
except RateLimitError as e:
    sleep(e.retry_after or backoff())
except AuthError:
    refresh_token()
except ServerError as e:
    if e.retriable:
        retry_with_backoff()
    else:
        raise
```

priya: perfect. I'll draft a short RFC and include suggested mappings + migration notes. tagging @sam_w @miguel for review.

deploy-bot: note — samples repo CI ran and added a failing test for current python SDK (test expects RateLimitError subclass). see: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/3872 :warning:

miguel: i'll pick up the CI failing test and wire the harness. will push a PR with exhaustive mapping matrix.

sam_w: sweet. can we target a docs PR in 2 weeks and SDK patch release in 3?

priya: assigning to eng-sdks board and adding to sprint backlog. thanks all :thumbsup:
